transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

I'm, uh... I'm a construction manager. And lately, I've been having some trouble at work. It's... well, whenever I have to get near a scaffold, or a roof edge, or one of the upper platforms... my head just tells me I'm about to go over. Even when I can see the rails are up. Even when I know the setup is safe. It's just... I can't do it.
Do you ever have episodes where you feel an intense fear or discomfort that reaches a peak within minutes?
I don't think so. I mean, I get scared when I'm up high, like I said, but... I don't know about episodes. I just try to stay away from the edge.
Is your fear limited to being in high places?
Yeah. Just... just the high places. I don't really have a problem with anything else.
Is your fear of being in high places affecting your work or personal relationships in any way?

Yeah... it's definitely affecting work. I've, uh... I've been avoiding a lot of the upper-level walk-throughs. I either put them off or just don't do them. It's gotten to the point where the crews and subcontractors are starting to question my calls. And... well, my employer's insurer actually pushed for an occupational health review because I wasn't getting the safety inspections done up there. So... yeah, it's a problem.
Have you ever had a sudden feeling of intense fear or discomfort that came on quickly?
Didn't you just ask me that? Uh... no. Not unless I'm looking over an edge or something. It doesn't just happen out of nowhere.
Is being near the edge or high place the only thing that triggers this fear of falling?
Yeah... pretty much just that. I don't know what else would do it. Just... being up high.
Have you ever felt a sudden, intense fear that wasn't related to being in a high place?
No. I just told you... it's only when I'm up high. That's it.
Is your fear of being in high places affecting your personal relationships or social life in any way?

Not my personal life, really. But... work. I'm a construction manager, so... it's a problem. I've, uh... I've been missing some of the upper-level walk-throughs. Or delaying them as long as I can. 

My crews and the subcontractors, they've... they've started questioning my calls because of it. And it got to the point where my employer's insurer actually pushed for an occupational health review. Just because I wasn't completing the key safety inspections up there. So... yeah. It's an issue.
Have you ever had a panic attack?
No. I don't think so. Just... what happens when I'm up high. But no.
How distressed do you feel when you're in a situation where you have to be in a high place?

I don't know about distressed. It's just... a strong reaction. 

The second I step onto the temporary stairs, or... even just walk toward an open upper floor... my chest tightens up. My hands get wet. It just feels like my legs might lock up on me before I can make myself take another step. That's pretty much what happens.
Are you avoiding any activities or places in your daily life because of your fear of heights?

Yeah. I guess so. Mostly at work, like I said. I've been... handing off the upper inspections to my foremen. Or I'll just move our meetings down to the ground level. 

If I absolutely have to go up... I make sure to keep someone right beside me. And I just rush through it as fast as I can. I'm pretty much... scared the whole time I'm up there. Just trying to get back down.
Are you avoiding any social activities or hobbies because of your fear of heights?
No. Not really. I don't... do much of that anyway. Just stay around the house mostly. So it doesn't really come up outside of work.
Are there any other areas of your life, besides work, where you feel like your fear of heights is holding you back?
Not that I can think of. Like I said, I just... I go to work, and I go home. My house is only one story, so... no. It's really just the job.
Do you feel anxious or worried about being in high places when you are not actually in a high place?
No. I don't really think about it unless I have to go up there.
Are there any everyday activities, outside of work, that you're unable to do because of your fear of heights?
No, not really. Like I said before, it's just work. I don't really do anything else where it would matter.
Are there any aspects of your daily routine, outside of work, that you feel are impacted by your fear of heights?
No. I mean... I feel like we just went over this. My routine is pretty much just work and home. So... no. Nothing else.
Are you feeling overwhelmed or unable to cope with your fear of heights in general?
I mean... no, not really. It's just... I just don't like being up high. I wouldn't say I'm overwhelmed. I just deal with it when I have to.
How long have you been experiencing this fear of being in high places?
About thirteen months. It started... after the stair tower accident.
Is there something specific about the stair tower accident that you think might have triggered your fear of heights?
I don't know. I mean... I fell. It was a bad fall. I guess that's enough to do it. I don't really know what else there is to say about it.
Do you think your fear of being in high places is related to a fear of having a panic attack or other incapacitating symptoms while in a high place?
No. I don't really think about panic attacks. I just... I just know I don't want to be up there. That's all.
